title: Linkerd Service Mesh, Rust Micro-Proxies & ServiceProfiles
summary: Master Linkerd lightweight service mesh operations: ultra-fast Rust micro-proxy (linkerd2-proxy) data planes, automatic zero-configuration mutual TLS (mTLS), ServiceProfile route classification, retry budgets, circuit breaking, and Linkerd Viz telemetry observability.
learningObjectives: Understand Linkerd micro-proxy (linkerd2-proxy) architecture in Rust and automatic zero-configuration mutual TLS.
Configure Linkerd ServiceProfiles with dynamic route classification and retry budgets to prevent cascading retry storms.
Utilize linkerd check and linkerd viz stat to monitor service mesh golden signals (success rate, RPS, latency).

curriculumModules.title: Rust Data Plane & Zero-Configuration mTLS
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Linkerd emphasizes simplicity and ultra-low resource utilization by using a purpose-built micro-proxy written in Rust (linkerd2-proxy) rather than general-purpose Envoy. It automatically provisions transient mutual TLS between meshed workloads with zero configuration, rotating short-lived cryptographic identities managed by the Linkerd Identity controller.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Deploy Linkerd in resource-constrained Kubernetes environments or low-latency microservices architectures where sub-millisecond proxy overhead and minimal memory consumption (<20MB per pod) are required.

curriculumModules.title: ServiceProfiles, Retry Budgets & TrafficSplit
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Linkerd ServiceProfiles define per-route client-side metrics, retries, and timeouts. Unlike naive infinite retries that trigger cascading overload, Linkerd retry budgets define a maximum ratio of additional retry requests (e.g. retryRatio: 0.2 allows at most 20% extra retry traffic), protecting struggling upstream services from collapse.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Author ServiceProfiles for all critical API endpoints, explicitly marking idempotent GET routes as isRetryable: true with bounded retryRatio budgets to safeguard upstream backends.

labs.title: Configuring Linkerd ServiceProfiles & Resilient Retry Budgets
labs.scenario: Define service resiliency for payment processing: author and apply a Linkerd ServiceProfile for payment-service.default.svc.cluster.local in namespace default. Configure a retry budget with retryRatio 0.2, minRetriesPerSecond 10, ttl 10s, and define route GetPayment matching regex /api/v1/payments.* with isRetryable set to true.
labs.productionContext: Retry budgets protect backend microservices from cascading retry storms during partial outages by strictly capping the proportion of retry requests proxies may issue.
objectives: Create and apply ServiceProfile payment-service.default.svc.cluster.local in default namespace.
Configure retryBudget with retryRatio 0.2 and minRetriesPerSecond 10.
Define route GetPayment matching pathRegex /api/v1/payments.* with isRetryable: true.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: linkerd.io/v1alpha2
kind: ServiceProfile
metadata:
  name: payment-service.default.svc.cluster.local
  namespace: default
spec:
  retryBudget:
    retryRatio: 0.2
    minRetriesPerSecond: 10
    ttl: 10s
  routes:
    - name: GetPayment
      condition:
        method: GET
        pathRegex: /api/v1/payments.*
      isRetryable: true

steps.title: Author ServiceProfile Manifest
steps.instruction: Save the ServiceProfile manifest with retryBudget and GetPayment route to /mesh/payment-serviceprofile.yaml.

steps.title: Apply ServiceProfile to Cluster
steps.instruction: Apply the ServiceProfile to namespace default.

validationRules.description: ServiceProfile payment-service exists in default namespace
validationRules.name: payment-service.default.svc.cluster.local
validationRules.remediation: Apply ServiceProfile payment-service.default.svc.cluster.local in default namespace

validationRules.name: payment-service.default.svc.cluster.local
validationRules.remediation: Define route named GetPayment in spec.routes

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /mesh/payment-serviceprofile.yaml
apiVersion: linkerd.io/v1alpha2
kind: ServiceProfile
metadata:
  name: payment-service.default.svc.cluster.local
  namespace: default
spec:
  retryBudget:
    retryRatio: 0.2
    minRetriesPerSecond: 10
    ttl: 10s
  routes:
    - name: GetPayment
      condition:
        method: GET
        pathRegex: /api/v1/payments.*
      isRetryable: true
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: ServiceProfile not found or retryRatio incorrect.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: The ServiceProfile name must match the full service FQDN payment-service.default.svc.cluster.local.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Verify metadata.name is payment-service.default.svc.cluster.local and re-apply.

labs.title: Auditing Mesh Control Plane Health and Golden Signals with Linkerd Viz
labs.scenario: Verify service mesh runtime health and live telemetry: execute linkerd check to validate control plane controller pods and API connectivity, then execute linkerd viz stat to inspect real-time success rates, requests per second (RPS), and P50-P99 latency distribution across meshed workloads.
labs.productionContext: Linkerd Viz telemetry provides instantaneous L7 golden signals without requiring dedicated Prometheus dashboards, making rapid diagnostics possible during production incidents.
objectives: Execute linkerd check to verify control plane and extension readiness.
Execute linkerd viz stat to inspect live golden signals and mesh success rates.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary design philosophy and architectural difference between Linkerd's data plane proxy (linkerd2-proxy) and Envoy?
options: Linkerd compiles all routing rules directly into the Linux eBPF kernel without any user-space proxy.

Linkerd uses a dedicated, ultra-lightweight micro-proxy written in Rust (linkerd2-proxy) designed specifically for service mesh sidecar operations with minimal memory (<20MB) and CPU footprint, whereas Envoy is a general-purpose C++ proxy with a broader feature set and higher memory usage.
Linkerd runs as a Python daemon process inside the control plane.
Linkerd requires manual SSH key exchange between pods to establish TLS tunnels.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: linkerd2-proxy is written in Rust to provide memory safety, deterministic low resource consumption (typically <20MB), and minimal latency overhead compared to general-purpose proxies.

assessmentQuestions.question: In a Linkerd ServiceProfile, what is the role of a retryBudget?
options: It limits the maximum monetary cost of cloud egress bandwidth.

It defines the maximum allowable ratio of retry requests (e.g. retryRatio: 0.2 allows at most 20% retries on top of normal traffic) to prevent cascading retry storms from overwhelming an already degraded upstream service.
It automatically increases Pod CPU requests whenever response latency exceeds 500ms.
It restarts any pod whose container memory exceeds the retry limit.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: A retry budget bounds the proportion of extra traffic proxies can send as retries. This prevents the catastrophic retry storm phenomenon where retries multiply and crash degraded backends.
